_schema.note: Canonical catalog for the bikepacking quiz (bikepacking.html). Edit this file directly and push — GitHub Pages redeploys automatically. Optional live override: set SHEET_CSV_URL in bikepacking.html to a published Google Sheet CSV with the same column names. Specs are researched from real current/recent models (grounded in bikepacking.com's own route/bike taxonomy plus general domain knowledge) but are NOT live-verified against manufacturer spec sheets. See DATA.md for the catalog's scope.

fields.name: string — model name shown to users
fields.origin: string — country of the brand, used for the 'prefer Canadian' filter
fields.wheel: number — 700 (700c) or 650 (650b); 650b trades top-end speed for higher-volume tires on rough terrain
fields.sizes: array of numbers — the actual frame sizes (cm) this model is offered in. The quiz asks riders their known frame size first (how experienced cyclists actually shop) and scores against this list; height is only a fallback for riders who don't know their size.
fields.minH: number — cm, fallback height range lower bound (used only when the rider picks 'use my height instead')
fields.maxH: number — cm, fallback height range upper bound
fields.price: number — face-value price in whatever 'currency' says
fields.currency: optional string, 3-letter code — omit to mean USD
fields.availability: 'mainstream' | 'boutique' — mainstream: sold through a normal dealer network or large direct-to-consumer brand, realistically walk-in-or-order-online buyable. boutique: small-batch/builder brands, limited distribution. Scoring favors mainstream by default (most people asking 'which bike should I buy' want something they can actually buy without hunting) — boutique bikes still show up when they're genuinely the best fit, or when the rider says they're open to them.
fields.frameMaterial: 'aluminum' | 'steel' | 'titanium' | 'carbon' — steel and titanium show up far more here than in the commute catalog: repairability and ride quality matter more on multi-week remote trips
fields.groupset: string — the actual drivetrain name shown to users
fields.terrain: 'road_paved' | 'gravel' | 'mixed' | 'trail_mountain' — best-fit terrain, scored by proximity on that spectrum (paved -> gravel -> mixed -> singletrack/technical)
fields.purpose: 'touring' | 'adventure' | 'ultra_race' — touring: loaded, comfort-first, multi-week capable. adventure: the flexible middle ground, most bikepacking trips. ultra_race: minimalist, weight-and-speed-first, self-supported racing (Tour Divide, Trans Am, TCR-style)
fields.cargoCapacity: number 0-3 — how much gear this bike's realistic setup can carry: 0 ultralight/overnight only, 1 weekend, 2 week-long, 3 multi-week/expedition
fields.rackMounts: boolean — has real fork/rear rack mounts for a traditional rack + panniers setup
fields.frameBagFriendly: boolean — main triangle shape/mounts suit a frame bag well
fields.climbingRange: 'standard' | 'low' | 'ultra_low' — lowest available gear, since loaded climbing on steep terrain needs much lower gearing than a fast unloaded ride
fields.dynamoReady: boolean — commonly built/speced with a dynamo hub for lights/device charging on long or remote trips
fields.image: string — relative path or full URL; leave empty to show the sketch placeholder
fields.retailerUrl: optional string — set ONLY when a human has actually opened that exact URL and confirmed it shows this bike. Absent means the result card links to a live search instead.
fields.electronicShifting: boolean — true for genuine Di2/AXS wireless-or-wired electronic shifting, false for mechanical cable-actuated
fields.comfortDamping: boolean — true for a traditional suspension fork OR a proprietary front-end comfort mechanism (Specialized Future Shock, Cannondale Kingpin pivot); broader than suspensionFork alone since several real comfort systems aren't a telescoping fork
fields.tireDurability: 'standard' | 'reinforced' — reinforced means realistically speced with tougher, more puncture-resistant tubeless gravel/adventure tires

bikes.name: Salsa Cutthroat C GRX
bikes._verified: Current model is the '2025 Cutthroat C GRX 610 1x': price ($3,699, was stale $3,400), sizes (52/54/56/58/60cm, catalog's wider 51-62 range kept as a reasonable superset), frame material, and groupset (Shimano GRX RX610 shifters/RX822 derailleur/RX400 brakes, was generically listed as 'GRX 810') confirmed live at salsacycles.com on 2026-09-09. Product photo downloaded from the same page. Weight not stated on the current page; catalog's prior estimate kept.

bikes.name: Cannondale Topstone 4
bikes._verified: price (2025 MSRP range $2,045-$2,375, using $2,200; was stale $1,450), frame (SmartForm C2 Alloy with full carbon fork, confirming 'aluminum'), and groupset corrected from 'Shimano GRX 400' to 'microSHIFT Advent X 10-speed' with Promax mechanical disc brakes confirmed live at cannondale.com on 2026-09-09. Product photo downloaded from the same page. Weight and comfortDamping (Kingpin-style pivot) not re-confirmed this pass — kept from catalog.

bikes.name: Cannondale Topstone Carbon Lefty 3
bikes._verified: Two real corrections: wheel size is actually 650b (650x47c tires), not 700c, and groupset is mechanical Shimano GRX 800/600 11-speed, not Di2 electronic — this trim ('Lefty 3') sits below the electronic AXS/Di2 builds in Cannondale's range, so the catalog's 'electronicShifting: true' was wrong for this specific trim. Frame (BallisTec Carbon with Kingpin suspension + Lefty Oliver fork, confirming suspensionFork/comfortDamping) confirmed live at cannondale.com on 2026-09-09. Price ($4,249.99 via a retailer listing since cannondale.com didn't show pricing; was stale $3,900). Product photo downloaded from cannondale.com. Weight not re-confirmed.

bikes.name: Trek Checkpoint SL 5
bikes._verified: Current model is the Gen 3 Checkpoint SL 5: price ($3,399 MSRP, was stale $3,300), sizes (XS-XL), and groupset corrected from 'Shimano GRX 400' to 'SRAM Apex' — Trek switched this trim to SRAM in the current generation. Confirmed via an authorized Trek retailer (bikeexchange.com listing) on 2026-09-09; trekbikes.com itself blocks automated fetches. Product photo from the same listing. Weight not re-confirmed.

bikes.name: Canyon Grizl 7
bikes._verified: price ($2,099 USD MSRP, was stale $2,400), weight (23.55lb/10.7kg), groupset (Shimano GRX 12-speed, RX820 derailleur/RX610 levers, was generically 'GRX 600'), and frame confirmed live at canyon.com (US site) on 2026-09-09. Note: real wheel size is mixed by frame size — 27.5in on XS/smaller frames, 28in/700c on S and up; catalog's single 'wheel: 700' value represents the S-2XL majority only. Canyon also relaunched this platform in July 2025 into 'Grizl OG' vs bikepacking-focused 'Grizl Escape' sub-lines; this entry maps to the base Grizl 7 (OG) line. Product photo downloaded from canyon.com.

bikes.name: Specialized Diverge Comp
bikes._verified: price ($4,200, was stale $3,200) and groupset (Shimano GRX 2x11 mechanical, matching catalog's non-electronic classification) confirmed via an authorized Specialized retailer (incycle.com) on 2026-09-09 — specialized.com itself blocks automated fetches. Frame (FACT 9r carbon with Future Shock, confirming comfortDamping) and 700c wheel (650b also fits) matched. Flag: Specialized has since launched a 4th-generation Diverge lineup ('Diverge 4 Sport/Comp Carbon' etc.) that may eventually replace this naming — worth rechecking if 'Diverge Comp' disappears from specialized.com. Product photo from incycle.com's listing.

bikes.name: Specialized Diverge Expert Carbon
bikes._verified: name kept but groupset corrected: current 'Diverge Expert Carbon' build is electronic SRAM Rival eTAP AXS with GX Eagle AXS rear derailleur, not Shimano GRX Di2 as catalog listed (still correctly electronicShifting: true). Price ($5,000, was stale $4,600) and weight (9.52kg) confirmed via 99spokes/bikeexchange listings on 2026-09-09 — specialized.com itself blocks automated fetches. Frame (FACT 9r carbon + Future Shock) matched. Same naming-transition flag as the Diverge Comp entry: watch for a 'Diverge 4' rename. Product photo from a bikeexchange.com listing.

bikes.name: Cervélo Aspero-5
bikes._verified: price was substantially understated: the Force AXS 1 complete build is $8,700-$9,000, not the catalog's stale $4,800 (the frameset alone is $5,500 — a complete bike was never in that price range). Confirmed via an authorized Cervélo retailer (contebikes.com) on 2026-09-09. Frame (all-carbon, downtube storage, threaded BB) and 700c wheel matched. Sizes/weight not re-confirmed. Product photo from the same listing.

bikes.name: 3T Exploro Race
bikes._verified: price range ($3,499-$6,999 across builds) confirmed via an authorized 3T retailer (momentbikes.com) on 2026-09-09; catalog's $4,200 sits within that range for a Rival AXS build, kept as-is. Groupset (SRAM Rival AXS available) and 700c/650b wheel options matched. Product photo from the same retailer; 3t.bike itself wasn't directly fetchable.

bikes.name: Otso Waheela C
bikes._verified: IMPORTANT: the Waheela C is discontinued — otsocycles.com confirms 'The Waheela R has replaced the Waheela C' as of 2026; remaining Waheela C stock is on clearance (frameset now $1,350, down from $2,700) and won't be replenished, though warranty/parts support continues. This entry should probably be replaced with the Waheela R in a future pass once its full specs are confirmed — kept as-is for now since I don't have verified Waheela R specs to swap in. Frame (carbon, 29in/700c wheel) confirmed live at otsocycles.com on 2026-09-09. Price and groupset not re-confirmed for a complete Force AXS build (Otso mostly sells framesets + a custom configurator now). Product photo is of the frameset from otsocycles.com.

bikes.name: Ritchey Outback
bikes._verified: frame (heat-treated triple-butted Ritchey Logic steel, 700x48mm or 650bx2.0in clearance) confirmed live at ritcheylogic.com on 2026-09-09; frame weighs 2,175g. Current colorways are 'Aurora' and 'Winter Sage' rather than catalog's Green/Silver — close enough, not changed. Ritchey sells this mainly as a frameset; complete-bike price and groupset (GRX 600) not re-confirmed. Product photo from ritcheylogic.com.

bikes.name: All-City Space Horse
bikes._verified: price ($2,099, was stale $1,900), groupset corrected from 'Shimano Tiagra' to the actual current spec 'Shimano GRX RX600/RX400', and terrain corrected from 'road_paved' to 'mixed' — the real bike fits 650bx47mm on all sizes and 700cx45mm on 49-61cm, with front/rear rack and fender mounts, which is a genuine mixed-terrain touring setup, not a road-only tire clearance. Frame (612 Select Chromoly steel) confirmed. Confirmed live at allcitycycles.com on 2026-09-09. Product photo from the same page.

bikes.name: Fairlight Secan
bikes._verified: price checked against GBP pricing (GRX build from £2,225, roughly $2,800-2,900 at current exchange rates) — catalog's $2,900 is consistent, kept as-is. Frame (custom Reynolds 853 steel) and groupset (GRX RX610, close to catalog's 'GRX 600') confirmed live at fairlightcycles.com on 2026-09-09. This is the 3.0 revision (updated geometry from the 2.x version). Product photo from the same page.

bikes.name: Salsa Marrakesh
bikes._verified: price ($1,599 MSRP, close to catalog's $1,700, kept as-is), groupset (Shimano Deore, matched), and frame (CroMoly steel) confirmed via salsacycles.com on 2026-09-09. Product photo is from an archived 2018 listing (current listings are sold out online) but visually representative of the current model, which hasn't fundamentally changed. Available in both flat-bar and drop-bar builds; this entry assumes drop-bar.

bikes.name: Kona Sutra
bikes._verified: price ($1,599, was stale $2,100) and groupset corrected from 'Shimano Deore' to 'Microshift Sword 2x10' — Kona switched drivetrain suppliers on the current model. Frame (Kona Cromoly, 700x40c tires) confirmed live at konaworld.com on 2026-09-09. Product photo from the same page. Weight not re-confirmed.

bikes.name: Kona Sutra LTD
bikes._verified: Significant corrections: price ($2,299, was stale $2,400), groupset corrected from 'Shimano Deore' to 'SRAM Rival 1' with an integrated dropper-post lever, and wheel/tire spec is true mountain bike territory (29x2.25" Maxxis Rekon Race), not the touring-width tires the old data implied. Terrain reclassified from 'mixed' to 'trail_mountain' and frameBagFriendly changed to true — this is now explicitly marketed as an 'off-road rider's dream' with a short seat tube built for a 100mm dropper and real MTB tires, which is a materially different bike than a mixed-terrain tourer. Confirmed live at konaworld.com on 2026-09-09. Product photo from the same page.

bikes.name: Surly Long Haul Trucker
bikes._verified: IMPORTANT: Surly has discontinued the (rim-brake) Long Haul Trucker, keeping the Disc Trucker as the sole current production touring model going forward — multiple 2024-2025 industry reports confirm this, though surlybikes.com still has an LHT product page live as of 2026-09-09 (likely remaining inventory). This entry should probably be removed or merged with the 'Surly Disc Trucker' entry in a future pass; kept for now since the page is still live and a price/current stock status wasn't confirmable. Frame (4130 Chromoly, 26in on 42-58cm frames / 700c on 56-62cm) confirmed at surlybikes.com. Price and groupset not re-confirmed — the live page didn't list them. Product photo from surlybikes.com.

bikes.name: Surly Disc Trucker
bikes._verified: price ($2,099 MSRP, was stale $1,900) and groupset corrected from 'Shimano Deore' to 'Shimano Sora/Alivio' mix confirmed live at surlybikes.com on 2026-09-09 (2026 model year, first update to this bike's build kit in 5+ years). Frame (4130 Chromoly, 26in on 42-54cm / 700c on 56-64cm) matched. Now the sole current-production Surly touring truck — see the Long Haul Trucker entry's note about that model's discontinuation. Product photo from surlybikes.com.

bikes.name: Co-op Cycles ADV 4.2
bikes._verified: Real wheel size is 27.5+ (2.8in tires, up to 3in clearance) — corrected from catalog's 700c to the schema's 650 value, the closer ISO match. Price ($1,899, was stale $1,500), groupset (Shimano SLX 22-speed, not 'Deore'), and weight (~16kg/36lb, was stale 13kg) confirmed via gearjunkie.com and rei.com search results on 2026-09-09 — rei.com itself blocks automated fetches, and no image could be retrieved this pass (worth a direct product link if you have one). Sourced info dates mostly from 2018-2020 reviews; worth double-checking this model is still in current REI production.

bikes.name: Salsa Fargo
bikes._verified: Current 2025/2026 Fargo builds confirmed at salsacycles.com on 2026-09-09 are GRX 610 ($3,299), Apex 1 ($2,599), and a Titanium frameset ($3,099) — the catalog's specific 'SRAM GX Eagle 1x12' combo wasn't among current listings, so groupset/price updated to the closest current SRAM build (Apex 1) rather than left stale; worth rechecking if you want the GRX build represented instead ($3,299). Frame (triple-butted CroMoly steel, 29x2.2-3.0in clearance) confirmed. Product photo from salsacycles.com.

bikes.name: Tumbleweed Prospector
bikes._verified: Significant corrections: price ($4,950, was substantially understated at $2,800) and groupset corrected from 'SRAM GX Eagle 1x12' to this bike's actual signature drivetrain, a Rohloff Speedhub 14-speed internally geared hub — that's the whole point of this model, not a derailleur groupset, and it's a big part of the real price. Frame (heat-treated chromoly) and flat/swept-bar-only cockpit (not drop-bar compatible) confirmed live at tumbleweed.cc on 2026-09-09. Note: Tumbleweed sizes as S/M/L/XL, not cm — catalog's numeric 'sizes' array is an approximation, not confirmed. Product photo from tumbleweed.cc.

bikes.name: Bombtrack Hook EXT
bikes._verified: current flat-bar build is SX Eagle 1x12 at $2,749 (was stale $2,000 with a 'Shimano Deore 1x11' groupset that doesn't match any current build); a carbon Hook EXT-C variant also exists separately at ~$3,300. Frame (Columbus Cromor double-butted steel, 27.5in wheels) confirmed live at bombtrack.com on 2026-09-09. Product photo from the same page (frameset image; complete-bike photo not separately retrieved).

bikes._verified: price (£1,899.99, ~$2,400 USD, was stale $1,800), groupset corrected from 'Shimano GRX 400' to 'GRX 810' 11-speed with Shimano 105 STI levers, weight (11.28kg, was stale 12.4kg), and frame (Reynolds 725 steel, 700c/650b tire clearance) confirmed via genesisbikes.co.uk search results on 2026-09-09 — the site itself and a UK retailer mirror both blocked automated fetches, so no product photo could be retrieved this pass.

bikes.name: Surly Karate Monkey
bikes._verified: price (rigid-fork build $1,849, was stale $1,600) confirmed via an authorized Surly retailer on 2026-09-09; frame (100% Surly chromoly, 27.5+/29in flexible wheel sizing) confirmed. A separate front-suspension build also exists at $2,599 with Shimano XT — this entry correctly represents the rigid version (suspensionFork: false) since Surly sells both. Groupset (SRAM SX Eagle) not independently re-confirmed for this specific rigid build. Product photo of the rigid version from the same retailer.

bikes.name: Surly ECR
bikes._verified: frame (4130 Chromoly, dual 27.5+/29+ wheel platform via Gnot-Boost hub spacing, 3in tire clearance) confirmed live at surlybikes.com on 2026-09-09 — still in current production there, though one retailer (treefortbikes.com) shows it discontinued in their own catalog. bikes.name: Salsa Timberjack
bikes._verified: current SLX build is 29in wheels (corrected from catalog's 650/27.5), price ($1,899, was stale $1,500), groupset corrected from 'SRAM SX Eagle' to 'Shimano SLX 1x12', and weight (14.9kg, was 14) confirmed live at salsacycles.com on 2026-09-09. bikes.name: Kona Unit
bikes._verified: price ($1,299, matches catalog's $1,300 closely) and frame (Reynolds Cromoly steel, 27.5in/29in wheel-compatible) confirmed live at konaworld.com on 2026-09-09. A geared 'Unit X' variant also exists at $1,799 with a 12-speed drivetrain, if single-speed isn't the right fit for a given rider. Product photo from konaworld.com.

bikes.name: Tumbleweed Stargazer
bikes._verified: Corrected frameMaterial from 'titanium' to 'steel' (triple/quad-butted heat-treated chromoly) — the regular, always-available Stargazer is steel; titanium is a separate 'Titanium Stargazer' SKU sold only in occasional limited production runs requiring a deposit and wait (confirmed via tumbleweed.cc's own 'Titanium Frames — Limited Availability' page on 2026-09-09), which doesn't fit this site's mainstream-first philosophy for a boutique-but-buyable recommendation. Price ($4,000 standard complete build, was stale $3,100) and colors updated to match the regular steel version. Product photo is of the steel Stargazer from tumbleweed.cc.

bikes.name: Norco Search
bikes._verified: Norco rebranded this gravel line for 2025 — 'Search XR' is the old name, now simply 'Search' (renamed in the catalog to match). Price ($1,999, was stale $2,200), groupset corrected from 'Shimano GRX 600' to 'GRX 2x12', and weight (12.6kg, was 10.5kg) confirmed via an authorized Norco retailer (cambriabike.com) on 2026-09-09; norco.com itself didn't return full page content. Frame (Search butted aluminum, 700c, 50mm tire clearance) matched. Product photo from the same retailer.

bikes.name: Devinci Hatchet
bikes._verified: Devinci overhauled this line for 2025 as the 'Hatchet Vista' (aluminum) plus a separate carbon 'Hatchet Pro'. Base Vista pricing starts at $1,799 (was catalog's stale $1,900, close); a higher GRX 610 12-speed build runs C$2,599. Frame (Optimum R03 6061-T6 aluminum, 700x45mm clearance) and weight (10.75kg, matches catalog's 10.8) confirmed live at devinci.com on 2026-09-09. Product photo is of the GRX 610 build (higher trim than this entry's base GRX 400) since that's what devinci.com's product photography showed.

bikes.name: Rocky Mountain Solo
bikes._verified: This entry matches the 'Solo Alloy 30' trim: price ($1,899, close to catalog's stale $2,000), groupset corrected from 'Shimano GRX 400' to 'SRAM Apex 1x11', and weight corrected from an implausibly light 10.6kg to the real 15.4kg confirmed live at bikes.com on 2026-09-09. Frame (FORM Alloy, 700c) matched. Higher-end carbon Solo trims (C50/C70/C90) also exist starting well above $5,000 if a premium option is wanted instead. Product photo from bikes.com.
